core_obligations: Reduce along the prime-to-l cover (proof lines 16026-16031): take f : V -> U finite etale of degree prime to l as produced by the cited lemma; the trace method gives maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism, so it suffices to prove finiteness of H^q(X, j_!f_*f^{-1}G).

Factor through Zariski's main theorem (proof lines 16031-16042): quasi-finiteness and separatedness of f allow a diagram with fbar : Y -> X finite and j' : V -> Y an open immersion with dense image; since f is finite and V is dense in Y one has V = U x_X Y.

Replace the extension along j (proof lines 16042-16045): by the shriek/pushforward lemma j_!f_*f^{-1}G = fbar_*j'_!f^{-1}G, so it suffices to treat the finite-type coefficient sheaf j'_!f^{-1}G on Y, by the finiteness lemma for finite pushforwards.

Reduce to the constant case (proof lines 16045-16049): the filtration of f^{-1}G supplied by the cover lemma, exactness of j'_!, and the short-exact-sequence finiteness lemma reduce the claim to the case F = j'_!M with M a finite Lambda-module, which is the cited somewhat-easier lemma.
proof_roadmap: Use the prime-to-l finite etale cover and the trace method to replace the coefficient sheaf by a pushforward it splits into.
Apply Zariski's main theorem to factor the cover through a finite morphism, and move the extension by zero across that finite morphism.
Filter the pulled-back sheaf, use exactness and the short-exact-sequence lemma, and finish with the constant-coefficient case.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a Noetherian ring Lambda, an algebraically closed field k, a separated finite type scheme X of dimension at most one over k, an open immersion j : U -> X with U connected, a prime l, n > 0, and a finite type locally constant sheaf G of Lambda-modules on U_etale annihilated by l^n, the groups H^q(X, j_!G) are finite Lambda-modules when l is prime to char(k), and when X is proper (statement lines 16010-16024). The proof (proof lines 16026-16059) is a four-step reduction: a prime-to-l finite etale cover via the trace method, Zariski's main theorem, moving the shriek extension across the resulting finite morphism, and filtering the coefficient sheaf down to the constant case. H2: a composite reduction with four independent inputs, all written out.
